purpose: Test whether the pinned frozen SigLIP2 representation contains substantially more answer-bearing digit information in a source-resolution oracle crop than in the corresponding oracle patch after the complete image is resized to 224 pixels.

probe.representation: one frozen final-layer patch feature at the programmatically known digit location
probe.global_arm: complete 1024-pixel image processed by the pinned 224-pixel processor, then oracle patch selected
probe.crop_arm: programmatic target panel cropped from the original 1024-pixel image, processed independently at 224 pixels, then oracle digit patch selected
probe.classifier: StandardScaler plus multinomial LogisticRegression with fixed C=1.0 and random_state=20260914

statistics.primary_delta: source_crop_224 row accuracy minus global_224 row accuracy

gate.rationale: The synthetic task is useful only if the same frozen encoder makes the oracle crop reliably readable while the globally resized oracle location remains substantially less informative.

claim_boundary: This train/development-only linear probe uses programmatic oracle locations and one deterministic synthetic rendering family. It can reject or admit the intended preprocessing information gap for mechanism development. It cannot establish free-form OCR, learned localization, natural-image transfer, language-model use of the crop, router quality, or superiority over another VLM.
